sentences: In \(\mathrm{CONGEST}_{b}\), each graph edge carries at most b bits per communication round.
The source studies detecting cliques with size at least four and up to order \(\sqrt{n}\), asking how far the round complexity exceeds its roughly \(\sqrt{n}/b\) lower-bound scale.
A linear-round algorithm leaves a substantial gap, particularly for fixed clique sizes.
The paper proves that its two-party vertex-partition method cannot establish the stronger lower bounds that would close that gap.
The project therefore calls for improved detection algorithms or new communication-hardness techniques that capture interactions among more than the two partitioned views.
